component.api.intro: Magma components are web components: custom elements you write like HTML tags, with any framework or without one. Props configure them, events tell you what happened, methods are functions you call on the element and slots take the content you put inside it.
component.api.props: Set a prop as an HTML attribute in the markup, or as a property from JavaScript. The Attribute column gives the name of the attribute, a dash when it is the same as the property; props without one, such as arrays and functions, are set from JavaScript only. To turn a boolean attribute off, remove it: never write `disabled="false"`.
component.slots.intro: Slots take the content you write between the tags of the component.
component.slots.default: The default slot, the one without a name, accepts plain text, unless its description says otherwise.
component.slots.label: When the component has a `label` prop too, prefer the prop.
component.slots.named: Content for a named slot goes on a direct child with the name of the slot in its `slot` attribute, such as `slot="{{name}}"`.

components.title: Components
components.description: How to start using the web components of Magma in Vanilla JS, React and Angular, and the list of all of them, generated from the installed package.
components.intro: Magma components are web components: custom elements you write like HTML tags, with any framework or without one. React and Angular get a wrapper package that turns them into components of their own.
components.quickStart.intro: Install the package for your framework, register the components you use and write them in your markup. Your choice of framework is kept for the other pages.
components.quickStart.installWrapper: Install the wrapper and the package it wraps:
components.quickStart.vanilla.register: In the entry point of the app, register the components you use: each `defineCustomElement*` function registers a component and the ones it contains.
components.quickStart.vanilla.use: Then write them like HTML tags:
components.quickStart.react.use: Import the components you use from the wrapper: importing one registers it.
components.quickStart.angular.register: Add the components you use to the `imports` of your component: each one registers itself.
components.quickStart.angular.use: Then write them in its template like HTML tags:
components.quickStart.next.title: Styles, fonts and icons
components.quickStart.next: The components also need Magma's styles and fonts, and mds-icon the icon files: the installation guide sets them up for each framework.

icons.page.mgg.title: Maggioli SVG Icons
icons.page.mgg.description: The icons of the Maggioli set, from @maggioli-design-system/svg-icons, ready to search and copy.
icons.page.mgg.intro: The Maggioli set, made for the products of Maggioli: public administration services, documents and their workflows, AI and more. The icons come from `@maggioli-design-system/svg-icons` and their slugs are `mgg/<name>`. Search them by name, or by their name in the icons package, and pick what a click copies.
icons.page.mi.title: Material Icons
icons.page.mi.description: Google's Material Icons in their four styles, a page for each category, ready to search and copy.
icons.page.mi.intro: Google's Material Icons, in four styles: pick one in the tabs, the slugs follow it, `mi/<style>/<name>`. They come from `@material-icons/svg`, the package iconsauce reads them from. Each category Google gives them has a page, in the list of the categories; the search looks through the whole set, also by tag.
icons.page.mdi.title: Material Design Icons
icons.page.mdi.description: The Material Design Icons of the Pictogrammers community, a page for each category, ready to search and copy.
icons.page.mdi.intro: The Material Design Icons of the Pictogrammers community, with their slugs `mdi/<name>`. They come from `@mdi/svg`, the package iconsauce reads them from. Each tag the community gives them is a category with a page, in the list of the categories: an icon can be in several, and the ones without a tag are in Other. The icons the community has deprecated, many brand logos among them, are only in Deprecated: better not to start using them. The search looks through the whole set, also by alias.

tokens.tier.internal.use: The pointers that themes and the contrast preference repoint. Not an API: never use them.
